sentences.pt: Gabriel e Lucas eram amigos desde a infância, em Fortaleza.
sentences.en: Gabriel and Lucas had been friends since childhood, in Fortaleza.

sentences.pt: Tinham estudado na mesma escola, jogado no mesmo time e, já adultos, continuavam a se ver todo sábado num boteco perto da praia.
sentences.en: They had studied at the same school, played on the same team and, now adults, still met every Saturday at a bar near the beach.

sentences.pt: Gabriel tinha virado professor de matemática; Lucas tinha uma pequena empresa de aplicativos.
sentences.en: Gabriel had become a math teacher; Lucas had a small app company.

sentences.pt: Numa sexta-feira, o governo anunciou uma lei polêmica: os celulares seriam proibidos em todas as escolas do país.
sentences.en: One Friday, the government announced a controversial law: cell phones would be banned in all the country's schools.

sentences.pt: No boteco, a conversa sobre a lei começou leve, mas logo ficou agitada.
sentences.en: At the bar, the conversation about the law started out light, but soon got heated.

sentences.pt: Gabriel estava convicto de que a lei era necessária.
sentences.en: Gabriel was convinced that the law was necessary.

sentences.pt: “Os meus alunos não conseguem ler um capítulo sem olhar o celular”, argumentou ele. “Eles estão ansiosos, dormem mal e não conversam uns com os outros.”
sentences.en: “My students can't read a chapter without looking at their phones,” he argued. “They're anxious, they sleep badly and they don't talk to each other.”

sentences.pt: Lucas, cético, achava a lei ingênua.
sentences.en: Lucas, skeptical, thought the law was naive.

sentences.pt: “Proibir é fácil. Difícil é ensinar os jovens a usar o celular com responsabilidade.”
sentences.en: “Banning is easy. What's hard is teaching young people to use their phones responsibly.”

sentences.pt: “Além disso, eles vão precisar disso no trabalho, quer a escola goste, quer não.”
sentences.en: “Besides, they're going to need it at work, whether the school likes it or not.”

sentences.pt: Gabriel tentou fundamentar a opinião dele com pesquisas, mas Lucas refutava cada dado.
sentences.en: Gabriel tried to back up his opinion with research, but Lucas refuted every piece of data.

sentences.pt: Os dois começaram a falar cada vez mais alto, e as pessoas das outras mesas olharam para eles.
sentences.en: The two started talking louder and louder, and people at the other tables looked at them.

sentences.pt: Então Lucas disse algo que não devia ter dito.
sentences.en: Then Lucas said something he shouldn't have said.

sentences.pt: “O problema não é o celular, Gabriel. O problema são professores que não sabem fazer uma aula interessante.”
sentences.en: “The problem isn't the phone, Gabriel. The problem is teachers who don't know how to make a class interesting.”

sentences.pt: Gabriel ficou quieto, pagou a conta dele e foi embora.
sentences.en: Gabriel went quiet, paid his bill and left.

sentences.pt: Durante as semanas que vieram depois, os dois não se falaram.
sentences.en: During the weeks that followed, the two didn't speak to each other.

sentences.pt: Gabriel sentia rancor e, ao mesmo tempo, saudade.
sentences.en: Gabriel felt resentment and, at the same time, missed his friend.

sentences.pt: O que doía não era a opinião de Lucas, mas o desprezo com que ele tinha falado da profissão dele.
sentences.en: What hurt wasn't Lucas's opinion, but the contempt with which he had spoken about his profession.

sentences.pt: Lucas, por sua vez, sentia remorso, mas era orgulhoso e não queria dar o braço a torcer.
sentences.en: Lucas, for his part, felt remorse, but he was proud and didn't want to admit he was wrong.

sentences.pt: Em março, a filha de Lucas, Júlia, de treze anos, começou a ter insônia e a chorar à noite.
sentences.en: In March, Lucas's thirteen-year-old daughter, Júlia, began to have insomnia and to cry at night.

sentences.pt: Lucas percebeu que ela passava a madrugada no celular, lendo mensagens horríveis de colegas da escola nas redes sociais.
sentences.en: Lucas realized she spent the early hours on her phone, reading horrible messages from schoolmates on social media.

sentences.pt: Pela primeira vez, ele entendeu o que Gabriel tentava dizer.
sentences.en: For the first time, he understood what Gabriel had been trying to say.

sentences.pt: Naquela noite, mandou uma mensagem curta ao amigo: “Você estava certo. E eu não devia ter dito aquilo. Desculpa.”
sentences.en: That night, he sent his friend a short message: “You were right. And I shouldn't have said that. Sorry.”

sentences.pt: Gabriel demorou duas horas para responder.
sentences.en: Gabriel took two hours to reply.

sentences.pt: Quando respondeu, não escreveu nada sobre a lei; perguntou apenas: “Como está a Júlia?”
sentences.en: When he did reply, he wrote nothing about the law; he only asked: “How's Júlia?”

sentences.pt: No sábado, voltaram ao boteco de sempre.
sentences.en: On Saturday, they went back to their usual bar.

sentences.pt: Lucas desabafou sobre a filha, e Gabriel ouviu com empatia, sem dizer que tinha avisado.
sentences.en: Lucas opened up about his daughter, and Gabriel listened with empathy, without saying he had warned him.

sentences.pt: Eles ainda não concordam sobre tudo: Lucas acha que a escola deveria ensinar mais e proibir menos.
sentences.en: They still don't agree on everything: Lucas thinks the school should teach more and ban less.

sentences.pt: Mas aprenderam a pesar os prós e os contras sem desprezo pelo ponto de vista do outro.
sentences.en: But they've learned to weigh up the pros and cons without contempt for each other's point of view.

sentences.pt: “A gente pode discordar”, disse Gabriel, levantando o copo, “contanto que a gente continue sentando nesta mesa todo sábado.”
sentences.en: “We can disagree,” said Gabriel, raising his glass, “as long as we keep sitting at this table every Saturday.”

questions.q: Qual era a opinião de Gabriel sobre a lei?
questions.qEn: What was Gabriel's opinion about the law?

questions.q: Por que Gabriel foi embora do boteco?
questions.qEn: Why did Gabriel leave the bar?
options: Porque Lucas falou mal dos professores.

questions.q: O que fez Lucas mudar de opinião?
questions.qEn: What made Lucas change his mind?
options: O problema da filha com o celular.

sentences.pt: Fazia vinte anos que Ricardo não voltava à cidade onde tinha nascido, no interior da Bahia.
sentences.en: Ricardo hadn't been back to the town where he was born, in the interior of Bahia, for twenty years.

sentences.pt: Ele só voltou por causa de uma notícia triste: o falecimento da mãe.
sentences.en: He only came back because of sad news: his mother's death.

sentences.pt: Durante a viagem de ônibus, sentiu uma angústia que não conseguia explicar.
sentences.en: During the bus trip, he felt an anguish he couldn't explain.

sentences.pt: Ele morava em São Paulo, tinha uma carreira de sucesso e quase nunca ligava para a família.
sentences.en: He lived in São Paulo, had a successful career and almost never called his family.

sentences.pt: Sempre dizia que estava ocupado e que no ano que vem iria visitar a mãe.
sentences.en: He always said he was busy and that next year he would visit his mother.

sentences.pt: Quando o ônibus chegou à rodoviária, ele reconheceu a praça, a igreja amarela e o calor seco da tarde.
sentences.en: When the bus arrived at the station, he recognized the square, the yellow church and the dry afternoon heat.

sentences.pt: Tudo parecia igual e, ao mesmo tempo, diferente.
sentences.en: Everything seemed the same and, at the same time, different.

sentences.pt: O irmão mais novo, Rodrigo, estava esperando na porta da casa.
sentences.en: His younger brother, Rodrigo, was waiting at the door of the house.

sentences.pt: Rodrigo tinha ficado na cidade e cuidado da mãe nos últimos anos, quando ela ficou debilitada.
sentences.en: Rodrigo had stayed in town and looked after their mother in recent years, when she grew frail.

sentences.pt: Os dois se olharam por um instante, sem saber o que dizer.
sentences.en: The two looked at each other for a moment, not knowing what to say.

sentences.pt: Ricardo percebeu no rosto do irmão um cansaço antigo e, talvez, ressentimento.
sentences.en: Ricardo noticed in his brother's face an old weariness and, perhaps, resentment.

sentences.pt: Na igreja, muitas pessoas que Ricardo não via desde a adolescência vieram falar com ele.
sentences.en: At the church, many people Ricardo hadn't seen since adolescence came to talk to him.

sentences.pt: Todos tinham uma história sobre a mãe: os bolos que ela fazia, os alunos que tinha ensinado a ler, as plantas que dava aos vizinhos.
sentences.en: Everyone had a story about his mother: the cakes she made, the students she had taught to read, the plants she gave the neighbors.

sentences.pt: Ricardo ouvia tudo comovido, mas também com vergonha.
sentences.en: Ricardo listened to it all, moved, but also ashamed.

sentences.pt: Aquelas pessoas conheciam a mãe dele melhor do que ele.
sentences.en: Those people knew his mother better than he did.

sentences.pt: À noite, os irmãos ficaram sozinhos na cozinha, entre as panelas e as fotos antigas.
sentences.en: At night, the brothers were alone in the kitchen, among the pots and the old photos.

sentences.pt: Rodrigo foi o primeiro a falar: “Ela perguntava por você todo domingo.”
sentences.en: Rodrigo was the first to speak: “She asked about you every Sunday.”

sentences.pt: Ele não disse aquilo com raiva, mas Ricardo sentiu um remorso enorme.
sentences.en: He didn't say it in anger, but Ricardo felt enormous remorse.

sentences.pt: “Eu sei. Eu sempre achava que ia ter mais tempo”, respondeu, e começou a chorar.
sentences.en: “I know. I always thought I'd have more time,” he replied, and began to cry.

sentences.pt: Rodrigo então desabafou: durante anos, tinha sentido raiva do irmão que foi embora e deixou tudo com ele.
sentences.en: Rodrigo then let it all out: for years he had felt anger toward the brother who left and left everything to him.

sentences.pt: “Eu também queria estudar em São Paulo, sabia?”
sentences.en: “I wanted to study in São Paulo too, you know?”

sentences.pt: Ricardo não sabia daquilo.
sentences.en: Ricardo hadn't known that.

sentences.pt: Pela primeira vez, ele olhou para o irmão com compaixão, e não como o caçula que nunca tinha saído da cidade.
sentences.en: For the first time, he looked at his brother with compassion, and not as the baby of the family who had never left town.

sentences.pt: Eles conversaram até a madrugada, rindo e chorando, lembrando da infância.
sentences.en: They talked until the early hours, laughing and crying, remembering their childhood.

sentences.pt: Antes de voltar para São Paulo, Ricardo disse ao irmão que ia pagar um curso para ele em Salvador, se ele quisesse.
sentences.en: Before going back to São Paulo, Ricardo told his brother he would pay for a course for him in Salvador, if he wanted.

sentences.pt: Rodrigo ficou relutante no começo, mas acabou concordando.
sentences.en: Rodrigo was reluctant at first, but ended up agreeing.

sentences.pt: Hoje, Ricardo volta à cidade pelo menos duas vezes por ano.
sentences.en: Today, Ricardo returns to the town at least twice a year.

sentences.pt: Ele ainda sente melancolia quando passa pela casa da mãe, que agora está fechada.
sentences.en: He still feels melancholy when he passes his mother's house, which is now closed up.

sentences.pt: Mas a nostalgia já não pesa como antes: virou uma saudade boa, daquelas que fazem a gente querer voltar.
sentences.en: But the nostalgia no longer weighs as it used to: it has turned into a good kind of longing, the kind that makes you want to go back.

questions.q: Por que Ricardo voltou à cidade?
questions.qEn: Why did Ricardo go back to the town?
options: Por causa do falecimento da mãe.

questions.q: Quem cuidou da mãe nos últimos anos?
questions.qEn: Who looked after the mother in recent years?

questions.q: O que Rodrigo contou a Ricardo?
options: Que também queria estudar em São Paulo.
